Reserved on 21.7.2016. Decided on: 04.8 .2016. . Ramesh Chand ....Petitione Versus State of H.P. ... Respondent. .................................................................................... of Coram The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ajay Mohan Goel, Judge.
texts.facts: 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 19.6.1995 T.S.Verma, Food Inspector, Kangra visited the Karyana shop of accused at around 2:30 p.m. situated at village Nangal Chowk and found that accused had stocked 10 kilograms of Haldi of Powder for sale to the general public. After serving notice of his intention to purchase the sample of Haldi powder on the rt accused, the Food Inspector purchased 600 Gms of Haldi powder from the accused against payment. Thereafter the said sample was divided into three equal parts and was put in dry and clean polythene bags which were made air tight and after labeling were wrapped in accordance with rules. Panchnama of the proceedings was also prepared which was witnessed by Shankar Dass and Ramesh Chand. Thereafter one part of the same was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis while remaining two parts were deposited in the office of LHA, Kangra in accordance with rules. Report dated 28.7.1995 of the Public Analyst declared the sample as adulterated, as the contents of the sample contained maize starch and un-permitted yellow oil soluble coal tar dye as an admixture, whereas Haldi powder should be free from foreign substances and added colouring matter. Food Analyst further observed that sale of powdered spices except under packed condition is prohibited under the provisions of Rule 49 (24) of the PFA Act. After receipt of the report of Food Analyst, the Food Inspector obtained the written consent from Chief Medical . Officer, Kangra and thereafter prosecution was launched against the accused. As sufficient grounds were found against accused, he was accordingly summoned and thereafter complainant record pre-charge evidence. As a prima-facie case was found against the accused under the provisions of Food Adulteration of Act read with Rules framed thereunder, charges were framed against him, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. Feeling aggrieved by the said two judgments passed by the learned courts below, the accused has preferred the present revision petition. texts.arguments: 7. In the present case, the accused has been convicted . for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a) (i) and (ii) of the PFA Act. Section 16 (1) (a)(i) and (ii) provides as under:- "16. Penalties.- (1) Subject to the provisions of sub -section (1- A), if any person,- (a) whether by himself or by any other person on of his behalf, imports into India or manufactures for sale, or stores, sells or distributes any article of food - (i) which is adulterated within the meaning of rt sub-clause (m) of Cl. (i-a) of Sec. 2 or misbranded within the meaning of Cl.(ix) of that section or the sale of which is prohibited under any provision of this Act or any rule made thereunder or by an order of the Food (Health) Authority; (ii) other than an article of food referred to in sub-section (i) in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or any rule made thereunder." 8. 9. Rule 49 (24) of the PFA Rules 1955 provides as under:- "(24) No person shall set powdered spices and condiments except under packed conditions." 10. 14. It has been further held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Janta Dal Vs. H.S. Chowdhury & others, 1992 (4) SCC 305 that the object of the revis ional jurisdiction was to confer power upon superior criminal Courts a kind of paternal or supervisory jurisdiction in order to correct miscarriage of justice arising from misconception of law, irregularity of procedure, neglect of proper precaution or apparent harshness of treatment which has resulted on the one hand, or on the other hand in some undeserved hardship to individuals. 15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ram Briksh Singh and others Vs. Ambika Yadav and another, (2004) 7 Supreme Court Cases 665, has again held that Revisional Court can interfere . with the findings of lower court where the Courts below have overlooked material evidence. 16.
